title: Common gate
description: A common-gate stage: the input drives the source, the gate is AC-grounded, and the output is taken at the drain. It presents a low input resistance (a current-mode input, so it is the classic input matching / current-buffer stage) and a non-inverting voltage gain $A_v = (g_m + g_{mb} + g_{ds})*par(R_{load}, 1/g_{ds})$ equal in magnitude to a common source. Its current transfer from source to drain is essentially unity, so it passes an input current to the load with a low input impedance. Both figures carry the source-body generator: the input drives the source, so $g_{mb}$ acts in parallel with $g_m$ rather than as a second-order correction. The input resistance is the DIVIDED form $R_{in} = (R_{load} + r_o)/(1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*r_o)$ — the drain load appears at the source divided by the device's own loop gain, which is why the popular $1/(g_m + g_{mb})$ shorthand reads low here. The device source sits at the input DC level $V_{in}$, so the bind declares $V_{SB} = V_{in}$ (body grounded); a table with no $g_{mb}$ column leaves these rows unresolved rather than quietly dropping the term.

params.name: R_load
params.note: load resistor at the drain: sets the gain

params.name: cdd_est
params.note: output-node parasitic estimate; refine from extraction

params.name: gm_id
params.note: lower gm/ID raises gm, so it lowers Rin (better matching) at the cost of headroom

rows.name: Rin
rows.note: low-frequency input resistance looking into the source, with the drain load carried through: (R_load + ro)/(1 + (gm + gmb)*ro). The finite ro couples the load back to the source, so a heavier R_load raises Rin — the 1/(gm + gmb) shorthand drops that and reads low (on a sky130 tt realization of this stage it gives 4.21 k against a measured 4.73 k)

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance this stage presents at its drain: the load resistor in parallel with the device output resistance. It holds for an ideal driving source; a real source impedance degenerates the device and raises it

rows.name: Av
rows.note: non-inverting gain: the source drive acts through gm, the source-body generator gmb, and the device's own gds in parallel, into the load paralleled with ro

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: device channel thermal density; a common-gate input also passes the source's own noise, which is set outside this stage

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
device saturated: the drain-to-source voltage is the drain level minus the source (input) level

the resistance looking into the source must meet the input-resistance budget. This is what a common gate is usually infeasible on: closing it takes proportionally more gm, i.e. more current, not a different topology
